bullets.title: NVDA: $100B+ OpenAI Ohio Data Center Commitment — Strategic Pivot Into Infrastructure
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced it will be the exclusive AI compute provider for SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, providing 8 IT-GW systems to OpenAI, with credit support for 4.25 IT-GW and an option for 3.75 IT-GW more. NVDA is investing $1.5B in SB Energy (a SoftBank unit), with the pair committing $4.2B total to develop 10 GW of energy infrastructure. OpenAI commitments reportedly represent ~$600B of NVIDIA compute through 2030; fintwit commentary notes this extends NVDA's moat from accelerators/networking into physical power inputs — a key constraint on AI revenue.

bullets.title: NVDA Strategic Risk: 20-Year Physical Infrastructure vs. Shorter Accelerator Useful Lives
bullets.body: One analyst flagged a material technology mismatch risk: physical data center infrastructure (cooling, power, networking) must be designed for a 20-year horizon, while NVIDIA GPU generations have substantially shorter useful lives. Future Nvidia systems may require different rack density, cooling, or power conversion, creating stranded capex risk for infrastructure locked in today. Separately, Groq raised $350M at $3.5B — down 50% from its September $6.9B valuation — with NVDA among investors.

bullets.title: NVDA and MU See $7M+ Bullish OTM Call Prints; NVDA Ranks #1 in Options Flow
bullets.body: Options flow trackers flagged $7M+ in short-dated OTM calls across NVDA and MU at Monday's open, described as unusually bullish for semiconductors. NVDA separately reported the most bullish options flow of any equity on the session.

bullets.title: SNDK Surges +42% Over 4 Days; Unusual Call Activity Detected
bullets.body: SanDisk (SNDK) extended its rally to +42.1% over the past four trading sessions, gaining 10% on Monday alone. Options traders flagged millions in unusual call prints in the name. HFTs were separately called out for widening bid-ask spreads on odd-lot trades in SNDK, disadvantaging retail.

bullets.title: MU Trades Above $1,000; +15% in One Month
bullets.body: Micron crossed $1,000/share on Monday, with one trader highlighting a 15% gain over the trailing month. Micron's Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana is confirmed to speak at the TomorrowX Summit on how AI is changing memory business models, with 'memory per FLOP' and 'tokens per watt' framed as key AI efficiency metrics.

bullets.title: AMD: Fabless Model Blurring as CapEx Hits $800M vs. $200-300M Expected
bullets.body: Analyst flagged that AMD is spending $800M in capex — well above the historical fabless range of $200-300M — suggesting fabless chip designers are now investing capital to secure scarce substrates and memory supply. AIDA64 also added AMD Zen 7 server support, roughly two years ahead of the expected EPYC Florence launch.

bullets.title: AMZN: Morgan Stanley $500 PT by End-2027; Anthropic Stake Worth $190B+
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its Amazon price target to $500 by end-2027, with the bull case contingent on AWS reaching $1T in annual revenue driven by AI compute demand. Separately, Amazon's stake in Anthropic is now estimated at $190B+, with some analysts calling base-case $250B ARR by 2027 achievable but the $400-500B scenario (Baker/Sacks forecast) too aggressive given compute and regulatory constraints.

bullets.title: AMAT: Heading Toward First-Ever $10B+ Revenue Quarter; China Recovery and ICAPS Tailwinds
bullets.body: Applied Materials is tracking toward its first $10B+ revenue quarter, with Q4 guidance pointing to 50%+ YoY growth at the midpoint. China business is returning to growth, and ICAPS recovery is underway. The stock sold off despite the print, with a reverse DCF framework cited to assess current valuation.

bullets.title: TTD vs APP: Leadership Contrasts Highlighted by LightShed
bullets.body: LightShed's analyst contrasted the management approaches of AppLovin's Foroughi (takes ownership of issues) versus Trade Desk's Jeff Green (attributes problems externally), with the implication that accountability culture is a differentiator.

bullets.title: COHR and LITE: Optical Sector Attach Rates Expected 'Very Low and Slow'
bullets.body: One analyst with prior buy-side optics experience warned that attach rates in the optical sector will be 'very low and slow,' cautioning that sell-side reports underestimate complexity and timing variability. Separately, a note flagged that 1.6T timeline delays would favor LITE and COHR, and OCP APAC Summit takeaways highlighted the scale-up networking transition from copper toward optics.

bullets.title: META: Sentiment Seen as Overly Negative Despite Strong Core Business and AI Tailwinds
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst argued META sentiment is 'extremely negative' even though the company has one of the strongest and stickiest core businesses in big tech, with AI and GenAI acting as meaningful unlocks for ad targeting and engagement. A separate user disclosed buying META shares.

bullets.title: UBER Partners With Zipline Targeting 1M Daily Drone Deliveries
bullets.body: Uber and Zipline announced a partnership targeting 1 million drone deliveries per day, with the goal of delivering items under 10 lbs within 15 minutes. One investor described UBER as among his 'two favorite investments' alongside Zipline.

bullets.title: 30-Year Treasury Hits 5.29-5.30%, Highest Since Pre-GFC
bullets.body: The US 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.29-5.30% — its highest level since the run-up to the 2008 financial crisis. Citadel Securities attributed the move to Fed policy sustaining elevated long-term yields despite moderating inflation; Goldman ruled out a September rate hike on weak jobs/consumption data, but prediction markets still price a 49% chance of a hike before 2027. Wells Fargo revised its forecast to now expect two 25bp hikes (2026 and 2027), lifting the fed funds target to 4.00-4.25%.

bullets.title: ECB and BTIG Warn of Equity Market Correction Risk
bullets.body: ECB economists warned AI-driven tech valuations are approaching dot-com bubble levels, flagging limited room to cut rates or deploy fiscal stimulus if a correction materializes. BTIG separately warned US stocks are entering the historically weakest period of midterm election years, with equal-weight S&P 500 typically seeing at least a 7% decline since 1990. Evercore countered by calling for the S&P 500 to reach 9,000 within 12 months (~16% upside).

bullets.title: Macro: SPX Vol at Historic Lows; 0DTE Straddle Priced at 29bps
bullets.body: The SPX 7790 0DTE straddle was priced at $22.7 (29bps), near Christmas Eve lows — the last time spot vol was this suppressed before a significant realized move. With the historical average daily SPX move at 68bps, one options strategist flagged vol pricing as dangerously complacent. Separately, $11.7M in far OTM VIX calls expiring in one month were detected.

bullets.title: Hormuz Strait: Zero Crossings, Iran Tanker Seizure, and 60-Day Truce Expiry
bullets.body: Hormuz Strait tanker crossings returned to zero per Bloomberg, and Iran seized a UAE-owned tanker in the strait. Brent crude rose 3% to $90.74/bbl and WTI rose 2% to $84.14 on the news. The 60-day US-Iran truce officially expired without agreement; Iran simultaneously shifted to a 'fully offensive' military posture and set a deadline of 'a few weeks' for the US to implement an MOU. The Pentagon reportedly concluded no current military plan can guarantee safe Hormuz shipping.

bullets.title: Xi-Trump Summit Confirmed for September 24 at the White House
bullets.body: The White House confirmed Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit the US September 23-25, skipping the UN General Assembly to focus on a bilateral summit with Trump on September 24. The visit is widely expected to address trade and tariff negotiations.

bullets.title: Unitree Humanoid IPO: 8,000x Oversubscribed, Implied $41B Opening Valuation
bullets.body: Chinese humanoid robotics firm Unitree is set to IPO on the 19th at a $9B valuation, with retail books oversubscribed more than 8,000x and an implied opening market cap of ~$41.66B (+363% premium). Fintwit commentary flagged the listing as signaling strong demand that could lift US-listed humanoid/robotics-adjacent names including NVDA and AMZN.

bullets.title: Big Tech Off-Balance-Sheet AI Commitments Estimated at $3T vs $600B Reported CapEx
bullets.body: One analyst highlighted that nine major tech companies have approximately $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments, far exceeding the $600B in reported capex — implying $2.4T in unrecognized obligations. The argument is that the AI arms race is creating enormous financial obligations not fully captured on balance sheets.

bullets.title: MRVL: UBS Cuts PT to $300 from $340
bullets.body: UBS lowered its Marvell Technology price target from $340 to $300, implying a meaningful downside revision relative to prior estimates.
